title: Kim and Button Town's Quietest Place
synopsis: The children add a bell, invisible socks and a bell-free resting spot to Button Town without asking everyone to play the same way.
continuity_state: Before: Button Town has a Doorway Tree, pretend post office and Lake Teacup; the real post-rain puddle may have dried; Kim carries three pebbles. After: The real puddle area is now mostly dry; the pretend lake remains a known feature. Kim names a visible grassy spot south of the Doorway Tree the Little Quiet Place. Its pillow icon enters a separate Button Town sketch kept with the other papers at Blue Door Cottage. No signs are left outside.

related_resources.reason: A child voices a preference and peers adapt a shared game; AAP general social-development guidance discusses cooperation and adult-supported social learning.
The comic imaginary shop is an example of collaborative pretend play rather than a structured therapy or evidence of an outcome.
